# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Respondents → the public account each story is based on

- Dwayne Hollis → [LYC] the group is "superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.)": an assistant super writes the log (the Current-solution escape). Author's invention beyond that.

Contractor operations leads (COMMERCIAL_B2B link, Part 3 only; no story by rule). Their picks are the author's, shaped by:

- Lena Brandt → the AEC engineer's comment that integration with existing products drives buying — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44043729 ; author's invention for the picks.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What would have made a difference

whys.g1: All three of us say the schedule is what really takes up the day and the log isn't the problem, so they belong together, and "Keeping the schedule is the real job" is how a super would put it.
whys.g2: There is no junk answer on this line; all three are straight answers about what the job actually demands.

whys.g1: All four of us are saying the schedule and the day's fires come ahead of the log, so one group fits every answer and the name is how a super would say it, even though Gary's and Denise's point about the log already being handled is only partly captured.
whys.g2: There is no junk answer on this line; all four are on-topic replies from people talking about their actual job.

whys.g1: One answer is about the schedule slipping when subs and the crane fall through and the other is about jobsite noise on a pour day, so they are different obstacles and leaving each on its own is how I'd sort them, with no group they should have gone in.
whys.g2: There is no junk answer on this line; both are real reasons from the job site, and nothing junk or off-topic was grouped.

founder.order_why: It runs naturally from naming the project and market through context, problem, solution and fit to who asks and who gets the link, with each step building on the one before.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 4 carry the same kicker and the same question, and each seed/card pair (5-6, 7-8) and tell-us/check pair (10-11, 13-14, 15-16) covers the same ground, though those are drafting then checking rather than a true repeat.
founder.missing: Nothing in the flow's screen titles asks who pays and at what price: I sell to the general contractor at about $1k per site per month while superintendents use it, so I would expect a screen for the buyer as distinct from the user and for the price, and at most 'Offer a pilot?' touches the commercial side.

PRIMARY.order_why: It checks that I'm on Procore or ACC and had notes to log, then shows the idea and moves from whether talking would work on site, to whether it would help, to whether I'd connect my account.
PRIMARY.missing: It never asked about the photos or how long getting the day's walks into the log takes me, or whether the log would hold up in a dispute with an owner over delays.

screens.why5: The steps match my product, but the belief drifts by leading with connecting, which I sell as a single click, instead of the real change: taking narrated videos on the walk.
screens.instead: What would they have to do to start? Take short videos or photos on walks and talk over them; check and fix the notes before they go out; get Procore or ACC connected, by them or the office. Belief: Most would take short videos and talk over them on their walks.

screens.why1: After I said what they would have to do to start, it makes sense to pick which of those steps Keel should test as the last solution belief.
screens.why2: Procore, ACC, walks and notes are all everyday words in my trade, and the belief and the 1-in-3 bar read clearly the first time.
screens.why3: A super knows if they would talk over videos or fix notes, but connecting to Procore or ACC is often up to the project admin or the contractor, so a super might have to guess.
screens.why4: The three options are distinct, in my words, and cover what a super has to do to start; no escape chip is needed because this is my own pick of a belief.
screens.why5: The wording of each option is mine, but the belief under test is connecting to Procore or ACC, while my own answer was taking short videos and talking over them on walks, which is the riskier adoption step.
screens.instead: Which of these do you most need to be true? Take short videos and talk over them on walks (selected; Keel will test: Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks) / Check and fix the notes before they go out / Connect it to Procore or ACC

screens.why1: Right after I've defined the solution and just before the study goes out, it makes sense to ask whether people who answer can ask to join a pilot; I charge per site and want a paid pilot on one site, so this is the obvious moment.
screens.why2: A pilot is a word I use every day with general contractors, and the hint says plainly that it is optional, comes after people answer and does not change their answers.
screens.why3: Whether to offer a pilot is my own decision as the founder, and I can make it on the spot from what I know about my product and sales.
screens.why4: All I see to act on is Continue, so the screen is workable but it does not make clear whether continuing means no pilot or what turning one on would look like.
screens.why5: Nothing here changes what I typed, and it neither alters my idea nor adds words to my study; the hint explicitly says answers stay untouched.
screens.instead: Offer a pilot on one site to people who finish the study? (Yes, let them ask to join / No, not now). Optional, and it does not change their answers.

screens.why1: Just before the study goes to strangers is the obvious point to settle who puts the questions to my superintendents, and nothing earlier asked it.
screens.why2: I get the question at once, but "this account runs on its own AI" needs a second read because it doesn't say whose AI it is or why that means tapping answers instead of being interviewed.
screens.why3: As the founder running this study, I can decide how it reaches supers, though I'd choose better knowing they may be reading it in the trailer at the end of a long day.
screens.why4: A preselected face gives me an easy default, but the hint makes the AI interviewer depend on credits without saying what they cost or clearly setting it against the read-and-tap option.
screens.why5: Nothing here rewrites my idea, my superintendents or my words about the product, so the study still means what I typed.
screens.instead: Who should ask your questions? Options: "Keel's AI interviewer (uses Keel credits)" / "No interviewer: people read the questions and tap their answers"

screens.why1: Choosing how strangers answer belongs just before sending, but it comes right after "Who should ask them your questions?", so it reads at first like the same choice asked again.
screens.why2: "Every answer in a quiet room. More than 9 in 10 where it is loud" never says it means how much of what people say gets caught, so I have to read it twice, though the rest is plain.
screens.why3: I know my supers are in trailers and on loud sites and whether they would rather tap or talk, so I can choose from what I know.
screens.why4: AI interviewer, text only or their choice covers the real options, they are distinct, and the credits note sits on the two that use credits.
screens.why5: Nothing here changes what I typed, and my pick of text only is on offer as a plain option.
screens.instead: How should they answer? AI interviewer: a face on video asks each question aloud and they talk, type or tap; it catches every word in a quiet room and more than 9 in 10 on a loud site (needs Keel's credits). Text only: they read each question and tap or type. Let them choose: they pick when they open the link (needs Keel's credits).

screens.why1: Right after choosing how people answer, the obvious last step before sending is deciding who gets the link.
screens.why2: The three choices read plainly on first pass to a founder who has been introduced to general contractors and supers, though 'Contacts page' only makes sense as a Keel screen, which is clear enough here.
screens.why3: I know whether I have supers' names from my own site visits and intros or would post in a group, so I can answer this from what I actually do.
screens.why4: Named people, a Keel search list and one open link are distinct and cover the ways I would reach superintendents, with nothing missing or odd and no escape chip needed.
screens.why5: My pick of people I know by name is kept as a one-link-per-person choice, and nothing of my product is altered or misstated.

screens.why1: As the first question, it makes sense to check what system my jobs run on before asking about my daily logs.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are everyday names on a commercial job, and I can answer this the moment I read it.
screens.why3: I know exactly what platform my job runs on because I upload my photos and logs to it.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it for a gate like this, and no escape is needed because I can't fail to know what my own job runs on.
screens.why5: It asks only about the platforms I use, and nothing about anyone's product or plan reaches me.
screens.why6: It is one short question with two options, and ACC said as three letters is how people in my trade say it.

screens.why1: After asking whether my jobs run on Procore or ACC, it makes sense to ask whether I recently had the day's walk notes to get into the log before asking for the story.
screens.why2: Site walk notes and logging are my everyday words, but "left to log" made me stop and wonder whether it means the normal end-of-day entry or a backlog I fell behind on.
screens.why3: I walk the site and do the daily log every working day, so I can answer this about the last week straight from memory.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, but a gate shouldn't carry escape chips, "I'd rather not say" isn't an allowed one, and "I can't recall one particular daily log" doesn't fit a yes-or-no about the last 5 days.
screens.why5: Nothing of a product leaks to me, but the founder's situation of photos and notes still to go into the daily log has shrunk to notes alone, dropping the photos that take up most of my time.
screens.why6: Said aloud, it is one short question ending in "Yes or no", which I can answer on one hearing, and it correctly speaks no escape for a gate.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, after your site walks, did you still have photos or notes to put in the daily log? Yes or no, with no escape chips.

screens.why1: I just said I run on Procore and had walk notes left to log, so showing me an idea about exactly that before Part 2 makes obvious sense.
screens.why2: Site walk, assignees, due dates, action items, crew, Procore and ACC are all words I use every day, so I get it on one read.
screens.why3: It is about my own walks, my crew and getting notes into Procore, so I can picture it against how I work now.
screens.why4: This is a card to read with no options, rows, chips or value box.
screens.why5: It is shown on purpose as an idea and stays clear and consistent, with no insider terms for people like me, though the last line only repeats what came before.
screens.why6: The short sentences say well and I can follow them once, but the last sentence is a long repeat of the card and 'Procore or ACC upload in one click' is a mouthful said aloud a second time.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco. During the site walk, you take short videos and talk over them. Fresco turns them into notes with photos, assignees and due dates, and texts the crew their action items. You send the notes to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe this would save you the hours of logging after the walk.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card, it makes sense to ask whether talking through my log would actually work on my site, since noise is the first thing I'd bring up.
screens.why2: The words are mine, but 'talked over the noise' doesn't say talked into what, so I have to rely on the card to know it means dictating the log and not talking to my crew.
screens.why3: I know how loud my site gets, but I do my daily log in the trailer at the end of the day, so I'd have to guess whether it means out on the walk or where I actually wrote it.
screens.why4: The four options run cleanly from easily to no without overlapping, they sound like how I'd answer, and 'I can't tell' fits if I've never tried it.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks beyond the name on the card, but the question only hints at speaking the log instead of typing it, so the founder's idea has drifted a little.
screens.why6: It's one short question with four short options I can hold after one hearing, and the escape comes last and says well.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. Where you did your site walk, could you have spoken your notes into your phone over the noise? Yes, easily; Yes, mostly; Only sometimes; or No. Or say I can't tell.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the question about my last daily log, it makes sense to ask whether Fresco would have made that log better.
screens.why2: I can answer it, but the "it" takes a second to connect back to my last daily log, and "go better" could mean faster or more accurate.
screens.why3: I do the daily log myself and know what the last one took, so I can judge it against what the card described.
screens.why4: The four options run cleanly from a lot better to worse without overlap, and "I can't tell" fits if I can't judge a tool I haven't used.
screens.why5: Fresco is named on purpose and nothing leaks, but "go better" loses the job of keeping an accurate record of the day's work.
screens.why6: It is one short question with four short options and one escape, so I could hear it once and answer, though the "it" leans on the earlier question.
screens.instead: Would Fresco have made your last daily log better, or not? A lot better; A little better; No difference; or Worse. Or say I can't tell.

screens.why1: After being shown the idea and asked if it would help, asking whether I'd hook it up to Procore or ACC is the obvious next thing to ask.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are what I work in every day and connecting an account is plain, though 'Fresco means connecting it' is slightly stiff.
screens.why3: I can say whether I'd want to, but on a GC's job the Procore integration is often the company's admin call, and the card only says 'Imagine Fresco', so I'd be partly guessing.
screens.why4: 'Probably not' and 'No' sit close together, and 'Only if it connected to my jobs without trouble' is odd because it hedges on connecting while the other options are plain answers, though 'I can't tell' fits as the escape.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks beyond the named idea, but 'Fresco means connecting it' reads like the maker's requirement stated in their words rather than something I'd say.
screens.why6: It is short and holds as a list of four, but 'Only if it connected to my jobs without trouble' is a mouthful beside the one-word options and 'Fresco means connecting it' sounds odd heard once.
screens.instead: Fresco has to connect to your Procore or ACC account. Would you connect it, or not? Yes; Only if the connection is easy; Probably not; or No. Or say I can't tell.
